summary: SIEM feed s171_triple is degraded with 3 faults: bursts of 3.62 Gbps overwhelm the 1 Gbps SIEM port, 5.6% of frames exceed 1518B and are dropped by NIC, and 7.4% duplicates waste capacity. Results in silent packet loss and reduced detection coverage.

findings.root_cause: Aggregate/burst traffic from packet broker exceeds single 1 Gbps SIEM ingest port with no load balancing or shaping. Peak 3.62 Gbps in 1ms bursts (362% of capacity) indicates multiple source ports aggregated to one tool port.
findings.impact_on_tool: SIEM NIC buffers overflow and drops packets during bursts (9 overloaded intervals). SIEM misses events, has incomplete flows/logs, and detection gaps during peak attacks.

recommended_fix.why: SIEM port is 1 Gbps but bursts hit 3.62 Gbps. Load-balancing across 4x1G ports or to higher-capacity ingest distributes bursts and prevents buffer drops; SIEM does not need both directions so per-flow hashing is safe.

findings.root_cause: Monitored network uses jumbo frames up to 8058 bytes, but packet broker forwards them unchanged to a 1 Gbps SIEM NIC limited to 1518 bytes. No slicing configured on broker egress.
findings.impact_on_tool: SIEM NIC silently drops all frames >1518B - 207 of 3725 frames (5.6%) are invisible to SIEM. Complete loss of visibility for large-frame flows, breaks detection and forensics.

recommended_fix.why: SIEM needs_full_payload=false, so payload can be truncated. Slicing at 1518B on packet broker ensures frames fit SIEM MTU and are not dropped, while preserving headers for SIEM correlation.

findings.root_cause: Same packets arriving via multiple SPAN/mirror paths or overlapping TAP aggregation without deduplication on packet broker. 276 of 3725 packets (7.4%) are duplicates above 5% threshold.
findings.impact_on_tool: Wastes 7.4% of scarce 1 Gbps SIEM capacity and processing, inflates event counts, skews SIEM analytics/correlation and can cause false positives while exacerbating overload.

recommended_fix.why: Enable packet-broker deduplication to drop duplicate copies before SIEM. Frees bandwidth for unique traffic and reduces load on already overloaded 1 Gbps port.
